question.problem:
Find, in radians to two decimal places, the argument of $z=-3+4\text{i}.$ 

**Hint**: The argument of a complex number is in the range $[0,2\pi ).$
question.worked_solution:
Let's plot $z$ in the complex plane.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14226152/assets/373ea8254a9816f67bfbcaf993348f409c1047284d09c43e5d41e68b15c5af58.png)

The complex number $z$ lies in the second quadrant of the complex plane. Therefore $\frac{\pi }{2}<\operatorname{arg}⁡(z)<\pi .$ If $\alpha $ is the angle that $z$ makes with the negative real axis, then

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{tan}⁡\alpha  & =\frac{4}{3} \\ \alpha  & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{4}{3}) \\  & ≈0.927\,30.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore

$$
\theta =\operatorname{arg}⁡(z)≈\pi -0.927\,30≈2.21
$$

to two decimal places.
